html:
The Beylik of Tunis was the state that ruled what is now Tunisia under the Husainid beys from 1705, nominally as part of the Ottoman Empire. The map shows it from 1715 to 1815.

The Ottomans had taken Tunis from the Hafsids in 1574. Power soon passed to local military rulers, and in 1705 Husayn ibn Ali founded the Husainid line, which reigned until 1957. The beys sent gifts to Istanbul but ran their own affairs and made their own treaties.

Tunis lived from farming, olive oil and trade, and also from the corsairs who seized European ships, though less than its neighbour Algiers. In the 1800s Ahmad Bey modernised the army and, in 1846, abolished slavery, one of the first Muslim countries to do so. Heavy debts to European banks followed, and in 1881 France made Tunis a protectorate; see Tunisia.
